precepts.text: Who is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of every creature: for by him were all things created, that are in heaven, and that are in earth, visible and invisible, whether they be thrones, or dominions, or principalities, or powers: all things were created by him, and for him. So Christ is the firstborn of every creature. By Christ were all things created in heaven and in earth. What is in heaven? All the angels, the host of heaven. Would Satan be a part of that? So who created those evil angels too? So now the creation is trying to tempt the creator. And look at the time that he came: after the forty days of fasting, in a weakened state while in the flesh. He said, oh, I can surely tempt him. This is what he created me to do.
precepts.point: You have to wonder why thoughts start to formulate in your mind that you have not thought about in years. Where does that come from? How do you remember your little girl from the fifth grade when you are fifty-nine years old and do not remember what you had for lunch yesterday? But when the tempter is coming upon you in your weakened state, he remembers everything, and he will whisper that memory into your ear and you will think it is your own thought. A sister gets into an argument with her husband, she wants to cool off, and Satan says, remember him back in the day, with that Studebaker, with the eight-track tape in there. Now you start thinking about him. Satan knows everything about you and him, from back in the day before you even met your husband, before you were even a thought, because you were his employee.

note.label: Stay in the Spirit

precepts.why:
“Who is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of every creature.” Christ is the firstborn of every single creature, the first created. “For by him were all things created, that are in heaven, and that are in earth, visible and invisible, whether they be thrones, or dominions, or principalities, or powers: all things were created by him, and for him.”

By Christ were all things created in heaven and in earth. What is in heaven? All the angels, the host of heaven. Would Satan be a part of that? So who created those evil angels too? Christ did. So in the wilderness the creation is trying to tempt the creator. Think about that.

Satan knew that was the creator. But look at the time he came: “when he had fasted forty days and forty nights, he was afterward an hungred.” He came after the forty days of fasting, in a weakened state while in the flesh, and said, oh, I can surely tempt him; this is what he created me to do. Christ answered him with the word: “It is written, Man shall not live by bread alone.”

The same thing applies among brothers and sisters. There is a time when you are in a weak state, spiritually, or physically from surgery or pain, and Satan comes: nobody called to check on you, but here I am; they don't know you like I know you. You argue with your spouse and go for a drive, and guess who is in the passenger seat. He whispers memories you haven't thought of in years, like Cleopus Jenkins back in 73 with that Studebaker and the eight-track tape, and you think it is your own thought. He knows everything about you, from before you met your husband, because you were his employee.

If Satan tried to tempt his own creator, how much more is he going to tempt us? That is why we stay in the spirit and answer him the way Christ did.

precepts.text: You can be blessed by God or you can be blessed by Satan. The devil took Christ to an exceeding high mountain, showed him all the kingdoms of the world and the glory of them, and said, All these things will I give thee. What is the stipulation? If thou wilt fall down and worship me. That is exactly what Revelation 13:2 describes: the dragon gave him his power and his seat and great authority.
precepts.point: And the dragon, which is Satan in this part right here, gave him his power, his armaments, and his seat, and great authority.

note.label: Agree Together | Bound Not Bondage

precepts.why:
Revelation 13:2 says “the dragon gave him his power, and his seat, and great authority.” How do we know that is what it is talking about? Because you can be blessed by God or you can be blessed by Satan, and some people do not understand that.

Matthew shows it: “the devil taketh him up into an exceeding high mountain, and sheweth him all the kingdoms of the world, and the glory of them; And saith unto him, All these things will I give thee, if thou wilt fall down and worship me.” What is the stipulation? “if thou wilt fall down and worship me.” Fall down and worship Satan, and he will give you all this power and authority.

That is exactly what we read at the bottom of Revelation 13:2: the dragon, which is Satan in this part, gave this last beast his power, his nuclear power and armaments, his seat, and great authority. The beast of seven heads and ten horns, the European powers with America as the eighth head, took the offer Christ refused.

And people are still taking it. On Venice Beach you have people who want to be blessed by Satan: women run through by every so-called movie or music producer who walks up and down that beach, still waiting to be discovered; a man about 90 years old playing the guitar, waiting to be seen by Rolling Stone magazine. People are delusional.

precepts.text: The land of Zabulon, and the land of Nephthalim, Galilee of the Gentiles. Zebulun and Naphtali are Israelite tribes of the northern kingdom.
precepts.point: The riches of the glory of this mystery among the Gentiles, which is Christ in you, the hope of glory. The Gentiles here are the northern kingdom, who can come back into the fold. You had no hope unless Christ came and died for us. There was no repentance, no reconciliation, lest it be for Christ.

note.label: The Colossians & The CHRISTIANS of America

precepts.why:
Colossians speaks of “the mystery which hath been hid from ages and from generations, but now is made manifest to his saints,” once again using that term saints, and then of “the riches of the glory of this mystery among the Gentiles.” There is a Christian out there watching who will say, see, Gentiles means the other nations. Matthew shows who the Gentiles are.

“The land of Zabulon, and the land of Nephthalim, by the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles.” Zebulun and Naphtali are Israelite tribes of the northern kingdom, and their land is called Galilee of the Gentiles.

So the mystery among the Gentiles is that the northern kingdom can come back into the fold: “which is Christ in you, the hope of glory.” We had no hope unless Christ came and died for us. There was no repentance and no reconciliation, except through Christ.

precepts.text: This is a prophecy written by Isaiah: he lightly afflicted the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali. Assyrian captivity, wham. The people that walked in darkness have seen a great light. Isaiah is prophesying and Matthew is revealing what it's really talking about.

note.label: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

precepts.why:
Some Israelites had come back to the land, and watch what they were calling part of the kingdom of Israel: “The land of Zabulon, and the land of Nephthalim, by the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles.” They were calling them Gentiles.

Isaiah wrote it first as prophecy: “when at the first he lightly afflicted the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali, and afterward did more grievously afflict her by the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, in Galilee of the nations.” That affliction is the Assyrian captivity: wham. Zebulun and Naphtali were carried away, and their land became Galilee of the nations, of the Gentiles.

Then Isaiah says what would come to them: “The people that walked in darkness have seen a great light: they that dwell in the land of the shadow of death, upon them hath the light shined.” Matthew gives it back as “The people which sat in darkness saw great light.” Isaiah is prophesying and Matthew is revealing what it is really talking about.

“From that time Jesus began to preach, and to say, Repent: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.” Christ was that great light spoken of, shining on the scattered tribes of Israel that had been made Gentiles.

To open the blind eyes, to bring out the prisoners from the prison, and them that sit in darkness out of the prison house. It's all going back to Matthew 4:15-16 and Isaiah 9:1-2.

note.label: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

precepts.why:
“I the Lord have called thee in righteousness, and will hold thine hand, and will keep thee, and give thee for a covenant of the people, for a light of the Gentiles.” The one given for a light is Christ, the great light that sprung up in Galilee.

Those Gentiles there are not talking about other nations. It is talking about what we just read in Matthew: “Galilee of the Gentiles”, the land of Zabulon and Nephthalim, the tribes of Israel carried away and called Gentiles.

Why is he sent? “To open the blind eyes, to bring out the prisoners from the prison, and them that sit in darkness out of the prison house.” Them that sit in darkness are the same “people which sat in darkness” in Matthew 4:16, the people that walked in darkness in Isaiah 9. It all goes back to Matthew 4:15-16 and Isaiah 9:1-2.

So when Christ began to preach “Repent: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand”, he was the covenant of the people and the light of the Gentiles, sent to Israel sitting in darkness to bring them out of the prison house.

note.label: Deceived by Enticing Words: Colossians 2

precepts.why:
Colossians 1:27 goes on: “To whom God would make known what is the riches of the glory of this mystery among the Gentiles.” Now you get to that word Gentiles and they go, ooh, we got you there. No, you ain’t got nobody. Matthew explains the Gentiles.

“The land of Zabulon, and the land of Nephthalim, by the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles.” Zabulon and Nephthalim are tribes of Israel, and their land is what they called “Galilee of the Gentiles.” Israelites living scattered among the nations were called Gentiles.

So the Gentiles that the mystery is regarding are not all races. When Paul speaks of the riches of the glory of this mystery “among the Gentiles”, he is speaking of Israelites that were called Gentiles, the same people the mystery was made manifest to as saints.

note.label: Joseph in Egypt: Then & Now

precepts.why:
“The land of Zabulon, and the land of Nephthalim, by the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles”. Zabulon and Nephthalim are tribes of the northern kingdom, and the scripture calls their land Galilee of the Gentiles. That is what they called the northern kingdom: the Gentiles. Christians have not figured that out yet.

So when Cornelius is brought in, he is not a Gentile of the nations. Look at where he was from: “a certain man in Cesarea called Cornelius”. On the map of the Holy Land, Caesarea sits right above Samaria on the left. That is Manasseh’s land. That is where Cornelius was from.

This is more proof that Cornelius was northern kingdom. You can jump up and call him a goy all you want to; we don’t give a damn. Do some research. Do some study.

Cornelius was “A devout man, and one that feared God with all his house”, an Israelite of the northern kingdom, a Gentile in the way the scripture uses the word, and his prayers and alms came up for a memorial before God.

note.label: Acts 10 Reloaded: Call No Man Common

precepts.why:
Matthew writes “The land of Zabulon, and the land of Nephthalim, by the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles”, and Isaiah had already written it: “when at the first he lightly afflicted the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali, and afterward did more grievously afflict her by the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, in Galilee of the nations.”

Matthew says “Galilee of the Gentiles”; Isaiah says “Galilee of the nations.” So the nations also means the Gentiles. Same land, same people, same word.

What we read in Matthew 4:15 was already recorded in the Old Testament. When the apostles and prophets spoke, they had to substantiate their points from what we call the Old Testament today. Whatever they said, they had to be able to justify it with that text. Matthew is not saying something new; he is showing the prophecy fulfilled.

This is the foundation for Acts 10. By the biblical text the Jews were going to be dispersed among the Gentiles and live like Gentiles, like strangers, like heathens. The New Testament shows Paul going out to find them scattered among the nations and bring them back to God, because the prophecy sent from the Old Testament was that the job was to raise up the 12 tribes of Israel again. The Gentiles of Galilee are Israelites that were scattered and cut off, and God is gathering them back.

precepts.point: Paul and Barnabas waxed bold: it was necessary that the word of God should first have been spoken to you, Judah; but seeing ye put it from you, lo, we turn to the Gentiles. Who are these Gentiles?

note.label: Recovering the Remnant: Worldwide Blitz

precepts.why:
Paul and Barnabas tell Judah, “It was necessary that the word of God should first have been spoken to you”, but the scribes and them were rejecting it, so “lo, we turn to the Gentiles.” Before that, those scattered abroad after the persecution about Stephen were “preaching the word to none but unto the Jews only”: only to the tribe of Judah. So who are the Gentiles they turned to?

Matthew answers it: “The land of Zabulon, and the land of Nephthalim, by the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles.” Zabulon and Nephthalim are tribes of the northern kingdom, and the scripture calls them Gentiles. When Paul and Barnabas turned to the Gentiles, they turned to the northern kingdom Israelites.

That is what the vision of Peter in Acts 10 was about. Peter said “it is an unlawful thing for a man that is a Jew to keep company, or come unto one of another nation”. Christians use that to say other races, but Ezekiel shows the two kingdoms were two nations: “they shall be no more two nations, neither shall they be divided into two kingdoms any more at all.” Judah was a nation and the kingdom of Israel, Ephraim and the rest, was a nation. And Peter’s own words about Cornelius and his kin folk are “The word which God sent unto the children of Israel, preaching peace by Jesus Christ”.

Acts 15 looks back on Acts 10: “After this I will return, and will build again the tabernacle of David, which is fallen down”. The kingdom was split, Judah, Benjamin and Levi on one side, Ephraim and the rest on the other. Turning to the Gentiles is God bringing the northern kingdom and the southern kingdom back together, the regathering of the twelve tribes.

note.label: Mindset Of A Leader, Actions Of A King

precepts.why:
Christ walked by the sea of Galilee and said to Peter and Andrew, “Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men.” Baruch shows where that invitation comes from.

“He hath found out all the way of knowledge, and hath given it unto Jacob his servant, and to Israel his beloved.” All the understanding and wisdom was given to us, not to the other nations. So there is no reason for you to sit on that wisdom and do nothing.

“Afterward did he shew himself upon earth, and conversed with men.” That is speaking of Christ. We are the only ones that have a God; the other nations do not. Our God saw us as so special that he showed himself on the earth. Our God, Emmanuel, walked with us and conversed with us. That goes back to Matthew 4 when he said “Follow me”: that was our leader telling us to follow him.

So we are not supposed to just sit here and do absolutely nothing. Our God saw fit to walk with us, teach us and guide us, and we have to do the same thing: teach our brothers and sisters and wake them up. The invitation is there, and like Peter and Andrew, who “straightway left their nets, and followed him”, we have to accept it.

note.label: Mindset Of A Leader, Actions Of A King

precepts.why:
This is our job. “And now, saith the Lord that formed me from the womb to be his servant, to bring Jacob again to him”. You were made to be the servant of God. You were made to do this work. You were not born to be a basketball player or a rapper. You were born to be a servant of God; that is our duty and our calling. “To bring Jacob again to him”: that is your commission.

“Though Israel be not gathered, yet shall I be glorious in the eyes of the Lord, and my God shall be my strength.”

“And he said, It is a light thing that thou shouldest be my servant to raise up the tribes of Jacob, and to restore the preserved of Israel”. Think about that: it is a light thing. It is the least you can do. The Lord sacrificed himself for you; our God came down and walked with us. It is a light thing to do the work of the Lord and go wake up your people.

“I will also give thee for a light to the Gentiles, that thou mayest be my salvation unto the end of the earth.” That is the same thing read in Matthew 4: Galilee of the Gentiles, the people that sat in darkness, saw great light. It is talking about Israel; we are to go to our brothers of the Northern Kingdom and be the light to the Gentiles, carrying on the mission God gave us.

precepts.text: Repent, for the kingdom of heaven is at hand. Being an Israelite in Christ is not dressing up, arguing with white folks in the street, or flexing; it is keeping the commandments with faith in his son so that we do not die when he returns. And no, it is not about multiple wives.
precepts.point: The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom; a good understanding have all they that do his commandments. It is biblically impossible to understand this Bible while refusing the laws of God. Everything you will see tonight comes from men who refuse to repent.

note.label: Fixx Ya Face Fridays | as Was Supposed!!

precepts.why:
“The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom: a good understanding have all they that do his commandments”. You cannot have a good understanding if you are not keeping the commandments. It is biblically impossible to understand this Bible while you are not observing the laws of God. There is no way around it. All the foolishness that gets exposed comes from those that refuse to repent and keep God's commandments.

That is why Christ's message from the start was this: “From that time Jesus began to preach, and to say, Repent: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.”

So many of our brothers and sisters out in the world have yet to come to grips with what we are here for. Being an Israelite in Christ is not about dressing up as an Israelite. It's not about arguing with white folks in the streets. It's not about flexing your muscles and trying to be a tough guy. And no, it is not about multiple wives.

Being an Israelite in Christ is about observing the Most High God's commandments and faith in his Son, so that we don't die when the Lord returns. The kingdom of heaven is at hand, and you are at risk if you do not repent and seek the kingdom. Point blank, period.

Those who deny Christ and deny keeping the commandments, because they want to fulfil their own lust, come up with absurd breakdowns of scripture. Without repentance there is no good understanding.

note.label: Donald Trump: the Sword of God

precepts.why:
After the dove landed on Christ and he had the spirit of the Lord, look how he began his ministry: “From that time Jesus began to preach, and to say, Repent: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.” The Lord is not willing that any should perish but that all should come to repentance, and Christ's first word is repent.

Now compare that to Christianity today. Do Christians teach like that? Hell no. They teach that the laws of God are done away with. So how do you escape the war and destruction to come if you teach the laws of God are done away? That ain't going to work. Say three Hail Marys and Christ will beam you up? That's what you think.

Paul says the same in Acts 17: “Forasmuch then as we are the offspring of God”, literally, “we ought not to think that the Godhead is like unto gold, or silver, or stone, graven by art and man’s device.” Those are idols. “And the times of this ignorance God winked at”: he had mercy, he was longsuffering with us. Then, “but now commandeth all men every where to repent”: all Israelite men everywhere.

So repentance is the answer to 2 Peter 3:9. Turn from your wicked ways, keep the commandments, gather together with your people as Zephaniah says, and seek the Lord, that it may be ye shall be hid in the day of the Lord's anger.

note.label: Transforming from Immorality into Beautiful Civility Part 2

precepts.why:
“And the Lord God called unto Adam, and said unto him, Where art thou?” Where are you, Adam? I put you down here to rule this earth, and now I'm looking for you. “And he said, I heard thy voice in the garden, and I was afraid, because I was naked”. He was afraid because he knew he had messed up. Naked means exposed to sin. They were not running around without clothes; they were never supposed to have the knowledge of sin, and now sin was in them. And Satan showed it to Eve first.

To show what Satan did, the class read how he tempted Christ, from Luke 4. Christ was “led by the Spirit into the wilderness, Being forty days tempted of the devil.” That is what brothers are going to go through: you will be tempted, and a man is supposed to be able to resist temptation. Women are not as strong as men, which is why she is supposed to look up to you. Christ resisted.

First the bread: “If thou be the Son of God, command this stone that it be made bread.” You have the power, so why sit here hungry? It was an attempt to make Christ forget why he was fasting, the way a cupboard full of food tempts you to forget your purpose. “It is written, That man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word of God.” Women will forget the course they are on, and that is why men have to protect her. She is in serious trouble without a husband.

Then Satan raised the stakes: “And the devil, taking him up into an high mountain, shewed unto him all the kingdoms of the world in a moment of time. And the devil said unto him, All this power will I give thee, and the glory of them: for that is delivered unto me; and to whomsoever I will I give it.” That is what Satan did to Eve. He likely hit her several times while she resisted, and then showed her something greater: you do not have to be under your husband; a time will come when you will be over him. He showed her America, with the man serving her, selling drugs for her, committing crimes for her, worshipping her. She spiritually fornicated with Satan, and brought it back to Adam with her beauty, without telling him about the death, and he took the bait.

When the reckoning came, Adam blamed her: “The woman whom thou gavest to be with me, she gave me of the tree, and I did eat.” It was not her fault; God put him over her, and Adam did not have to listen. Then she blamed the serpent: “The serpent beguiled me, and I did eat.” The family unit was attacked. The family is the backbone of the nation, and once husband and wife violate each other's roles they work against each other instead of for each other, and the children come out confused and troubled. That destruction came down through the generations to husbands and wives today. Men must restore the order and bring back our civility.

How did Israelites come to be called Gentiles? In the days of the Maccabees, “according to the commandment they put to death certain women, that had caused their children to be circumcised. And they hanged the infants about their necks”. They were enforcing it: you could not be circumcised; you had to be like the Gentiles. They were hanging babies. So what is the next generation going to be? Uncircumcised. And the next one, uncircumcised, not keeping the laws, profaning the Sabbath, calling themselves and being called Gentiles.

That is how Ephesians 2 has to be understood.

That region became known as the land of the Gentiles, as you read in the gospel: “The land of Zabulon, and the land of Nephthalim, by the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles”. Beyond Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles: the east-side territory on the other side Jordan toward the rising of the sun.

precepts.why:
Christ was led up of the Spirit into the wilderness to be tempted, and after fasting forty days and forty nights he was an hungred. The tempter came at the weakest point and went at the flesh first: “command that these stones be made bread.”

John lays out everything the enemy uses: “For all that is in the world, the lust of the flesh, and the lust of the eyes, and the pride of life, is not of the Father, but is of the world.” Bread for a hungry man is the lust of the flesh, and that is where the devil began.

This is the same set of temptations the man and the woman met in the garden, and they run through everything the enemy uses: the flesh, the eyes, and pride. “Love not the world, neither the things that are in the world. If any man love the world, the love of the Father is not in him.” Christ, hungry in the wilderness, did not love the world, and so the love of the Father was in him.

Moses tells Israel why the Most High “suffered thee to hunger, and fed thee with manna”: “that he might make thee know” this very thing. Israel was made hungry in the wilderness to learn it, and Christ, hungry in the wilderness, lived by it. He did not answer the devil with his own words but with the law, “It is written”.

The devil went at the flesh with bread. But the flesh profits nothing; it is the spirit that quickens, and the spirit is strengthened by the word, which is spirit and life. That is why Christ answered hunger with “every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of God” rather than with bread. Man lives by the word, and the word is what the spirit lives on.
